reasoning: Both sets cover all three stages and use the same skeleton: a frozen interface task, spines, wiring and system tasks, a dependency graph and packets. B is closer to the ground truth and plans its milestones better. A's fish tank is a square, but the user asked for a circular tank. B has a circular tank scored by survival time, a single learning predator against a school of foraging prey, an explicit ladder through tabular, DQN, REINFORCE, PPO and opponent-pool self-play, a correct truncation-versus-termination split, and concrete golden cases with worked numbers (GAE, clipping, views, reflection). A splits Snake into M1 'Train and evaluate', which has no replay viewer and only a spine DQN without a replay buffer, and M2 'See, check and explain', which holds the replay, the reference check and the notes. That M2 is the kind of leftover milestone the rubric penalises, and it leaves the stage's promised replay out of the first milestone. A also has a spine that builds another component's writer (T09 builds runlog/writer.py), stale open questions and a kept Retired section. B's main faults are process narration in the architecture ('adopted before M1 is built', 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change'), a brief line ('Not doing: Designing future environments now') that the spec contradicts, an untyped `targets` boundary in PL-04, and an M1 that is very large. In both sets the spine packets leave out types the spine needs.
